ruling.recommended_action: Reject the rider's $5.00 waiver request: the driver-cancelled no-show charge is valid under NS-1 (arrival confirmed at 12:17:10 within 39 m, continuous in-radius wait to cancellation well past the 8-minute case threshold). No refund and no account action — record the fee as the valid no-show charge.
ruling.reasoning:
F4 and F5 show the driver, not the rider, cancelled the booking at 12:25:20, so this driver-initiated no-show claim is routed exclusively through the no-show branch by NS-0 [F4][F5][NS-0]. The trace settles that branch's elements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" himself at 12:17:10, 39 m from the pickup (closest approach 6 m) [F6][F1], and remained continuously inside the 200 m radius for 490 s (8 min 10 s) after the tap, past the case record's 8-minute no-show threshold, with no GPS hole across the wait [F6][F2][F3]. On those settled facts NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are met, so the no-show cancellation charge stands [F6][F2][F3][NS-1].

Two readings are put forward for the $5.00 on the fare record [F7][F4]. The rider reads it as the "Waiting Time Fee" and argues it fails NS-6 because the trip was never completed and no drop-off tap occurred [F4][F10][F7][NS-6]. That reading cannot be right: NS-6 governs a $5.00 waiting fee added at drop-off after a completed trip, and here there was no trip at all [F4][F5][F10][NS-6]; a clause whose conditions cannot apply cannot be the clause that authorises a charge, and its failure does not waive a charge that another clause does authorise [NS-6][NS-1]. The amount actually charged is settled by the trace's case parameter as the cancellation fee for a driver-cancelled no-show ($5.00), and NS-0 makes NS-1/NS-2 the only route by which such a fee can arise [F7][F4][NS-0][NS-1].

The rider's strongest textual point — that NS-1 speaks of $6.61 while the record shows $5.00 [F7][F4] — goes to quantum and labelling, not to whether a charge is owed [NS-0][NS-1][NS-2]. NS-2, the only provision that would reverse the charge, applies solely where one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails [F6][F2][F3][NS-2]; all three pass on this record, and both advocates conceded them in rebuttal [F6][F3][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider's account that he had already cancelled by the time she came out supports only that she did not appear; her own closing message "8 min up, cancelling the trip" and the complete, timestamped two-message record with no rider reply corroborate the no-show reading [F10][F11][F9][F4][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement claiming he "waited the full 8 minutes" [F12] is not relied on and is not needed: the GPS and timeline records independently establish the wait, and a statement cannot substitute for the record [F6][F2][F3][NS-1]. The profiles — rider 1 dispute/0 upheld, driver 3 disputes/2 upheld, both no-show [F16][F17] — decide nothing here and no flag is raised under NS-2, whose flag attaches only when NS-1 fails, which it does not [NS-2][NS-1].

No detour segment exists in this case, so RD-2's rate arithmetic has no application and no amount is computed [F7][F4][RD-2]. There is no safety or escalation trigger: the chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, abuse or driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][F11].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's own concession that the driver stayed 9 min 35 s within 200 m [F2] and 8 min 10 s in radius after the tap [F6] establishes NS-1 (iii), not a defect in the charge; the objection that 'a fee was levied at all' is answered by NS-1/NS-0, which authorise the driver-cancelled no-show charge [F6][F2][NS-1][NS-0].

The recorded $5.00 cancellation amount [F7][F4] cannot be routed to NS-6: NS-6 requires a completed trip, boarding and a drop-off tap, none of which occurred on a driver-cancelled booking [F4][F5][F10][NS-6]; the case-record parameter fixes $5.00 as the no-show cancellation charge and NS-0 routes it through NS-1 [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-1].

The absence of a completed trip and of any drop-off tap [F4][F5][F10] defeats the applicability of NS-6 rather than waiving the charge; the charge is assessed under NS-1, whose conditions are all met [F6][F2][F3][NS-6][NS-1].

The rider's request for a full refund inverts NS-2: NS-2 applies only where one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails [F6][F2][F3][NS-2], and the complete, timestamped two-message record with no rider reply [F11][F9][F10] corroborates rather than negates the no-show finding [NS-1].

The rider expressly offers the profiles only as an additional action, and profile facts cannot decide a case; NS-2's account flag attaches only where NS-1 fails, which it does not [F17][F16][F6][F2][F3][NS-2][NS-1].

The driver's characterisation of the $5.00 as a no-show cancellation charge is accepted in substance but cannot rest on his own say-so; the charge stands because the case-record parameter sets $5.00 for this branch and NS-1's three conditions are met on the GPS/timeline record [F7][F4][F6][F2][F3][NS-1][NS-0].
